# buildkite_deployment_artifact (Resource)

~> **Preview:** Buildkite Releases is a preview feature and is not yet generally available.

Manages a Deployment Artifact registration, not build job artifacts or artifact publications.

Destroy archives the registration, preserving history and reserving its name. Create rejects existing active or archived names by default. For manual recovery, unarchive the registration and import its UUID, or set `allow_unarchive_on_create = true` to restore a matching archived registration. Refresh treats an archived registration as absent; it never unarchives during read.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "buildkite_deployment_artifact" "api" {
  name = "payments-api"
}

# Destroy archives this registration and reserves its name.
# Set allow_unarchive_on_create = true only to restore an archived registration.
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The registration name. Unique within the organization, including archived registrations. Renamed in place.

### Optional

- `allow_unarchive_on_create` (Boolean) Allow create to restore an archived registration with the same name, retaining its UUID and history. Defaults to `false`. Never adopts an active registration. This flag has no effect on updates or refresh.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The GraphQL ID of the registration.
- `uuid` (String) The UUID of the registration, used for import.

## Import

Using `terraform import`, import resources using the `id`. For example:
```shell
# Unarchive the registration first if archived, then import its UUID (not the GraphQL ID).
terraform import buildkite_deployment_artifact.api 01a1b2c3-4d5e-7f60-8a1b-2c3d4e5f6a7b
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import instances using the `id`. For example:
```terraform
import {
  to = buildkite_deployment_artifact.api
  id = "01a1b2c3-4d5e-7f60-8a1b-2c3d4e5f6a7b"
}
```
